subject: Synthesis: discovery follow-up & head-to-head test plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@beaconhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — recap and proposed next tests

Jordan — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Peak inference latency spikes during nightly batch jobs and day-time traffic bursts (user-facing latency > 400ms p95).
- Unit economics: cost per inference and predictability during burst windows (primary ask: reduce token $/1000).
- Rollout friction: current model updates require heavy infra ops; team wants safer rollouts and rollback.
- Audit/compliance: need detailed request-level audit logs and tenant isolation for PHI.

Goals you’re trying to achieve (summary):
1) 3-month POC with measurable SLAs (p95 latency target < 200ms for inference path; 99.9% availability).
2) Integration with your ML platform (feature-flagged rollout, KV cache support).
3) Clear comparison vs two incumbent vendors on cost and observability.

Decision criteria we should capture in the test plan:
- Latency (p50/p95/p99) under representative traffic shapes (burst and sustained).
- Throughput: sustained qps and warm-up behavior.
- Cost model: effective $/1M tokens including batching and quantization tradeoffs.
- Security: VPC/on-prem options, KMS integration, audit log fidelity and retention.
- Operational controls: canary/A-B rollouts, auto-fallback to smaller models.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Attached: discovery notes + a starter criteria spreadsheet (beacon-criteria-spreadsheet.xlsx). Please review and annotate the cells you care most about.
- We propose a technical deep-dive on Mon, Jun 14 10:00 AM PT to walk the test matrix and owners.
- Confirm the test dataset (anonymized logs + the 10 representative prompts you mentioned) — can Anya share ETA for that?
- We'll include AltServe and NimbusAI as baseline competitors; internal team recommends adding Nebula Labs for the parity check.

Attachments: 20270611-discovery-notes.pdf, beacon-criteria-spreadsheet.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite after you confirm the deep-dive slot.

—
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0129
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@beaconhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — recap and proposed next tests

Rachel — really helpful recap, thanks. A few clarifications and answers from our side: 

Clarifications / additions:
- Confirming the biggest immediate customer impact is the daytime web latency spikes (we see p95 ~420ms now). Nightly batch job interference is secondary but important during model retrains.
- Procurement timeline: goal is to pick a vendor by end of Q3; procurement and security review will run in parallel.

Questions for the test plan:
1) Can you include cold-cache and warm-cache runs (we care about cold start behavior for new deployments)?
2) Do you support multi-tenant KMS and HSM integration for key separation?
3) For the cost column, please include an apples-to-apples projection for our 1M monthly tokens with baseline batching assumptions.

Target test thresholds we’d like to see (to consider Redwood a frontrunner):
- p95 inference latency < 200ms at 100 qps sustained (50-token average response).
- Throughput scaling to 500 qps with graceful degradation (no error rate >0.5%).

I’ll confirm the anonymized sample logs and put Anya on a share to your Drive folder. Also looping in our ML Ops lead Anya Patel (cc’d) — she’ll own test data and access.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.inference>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — recap and proposed next tests (internal ops notes)

Team — quick internal note with a proposed test matrix and owners before we lock the agenda for Mon. I’ll run the first round of smoke tests if we agree on schedule.

Proposed vendor matrix (baseline):
- Redwood (control)
- AltServe (customer incumbent)
- NimbusAI (competing managed provider)
- Nebula Labs (self-hosted / hybrid)

Minimum runbook for each vendor (suggested):
1) Cold-start latency: 10 cold restarts, measure p50/p95/p99. Owner: Marissa.
2) Warm-cached throughput: ramp 0 -> 500 qps over 10 minutes, measure tail latency and error rate. Owner: Camila.
3) Batch-size sensitivity: test batch sizes 1/4/8/16, measure effective tokens/sec and cost estimate. Owner: Rachel.
4) KV cache efficacy: run prefix + KV load patterns and measure token reduction and latency. Owner: Camila.
5) Observability & traces: validate request-level logs, sampling, and retention policies (security checklist). Owner: Marissa.

Open probes we should add to the spreadsheet:
- Does vendor support per-request KMS scoping? (security)
- How fast are model swaps (time to rollback to previous model)?
- Warm-up profile after a redeploy (number of tokens before steady state).


Scheduling: propose we run the first vendor (Redwood control) the week of Jun 21 — gives time for Beacon to share test data. I’ll prepare the smoke scripts and a results template to capture metrics and screenshots.


Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
